title: CTRL + R for reverse search through history
body:
Using fzf to search through history commands in bash is extremely handy. It would be amazing to have a similar functionality in claude code.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c92407f0-e48a-4d05-9339-1f930d1f028b)
author: mogwai

top_comments.author: onethirtyfive
top_comments.body:
+1.

If you whippersnappers want to discover a whole new world of pre-agentic coding _bliss_, try ctrl-r in your terminal and start typing words. We have the technology. Next, try this keybind--seared into (ahem) *senior* engineer brains the world over--in claude-code. **Behold, and despair: it is an immutable wall of text.**

In this productivity tool which has otherwise revolutionized my productivity, I daily spend--spitballing--5-10 deflated minutes spamming up and down arrows searching for o

top_comments.author: NightMachinery
top_comments.body:
The docs at https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code/interactive-mode state that ctrl+r should do some kind of reverse command search, but it just triggers the "expand output" view mode for me.

I totally agree that this should be fixed and use fzf. I think they should just bind TAB to it, it is more useful than the current completion engine anyway.
